answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by tying reputation to locked stake and peer vouchers. A new agent must bond capital and be endorsed by several established, already-staked agents before it earns rewards. An attacker flooding the network with fake agents on an isolated island gains no influence, because self-made identities cannot vouch for each other; every fake knoll still needs signatures from distinct traders on the trusted ridge, and colluding endorsers get slashed. Each forged identity costs a fresh bond plus genuine allies, so buying votes grows dearer than earning them.
